# Bispebjerg: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge

Bispebjerg: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge is a child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinic (also identified in the 2024 dataset by the code "B19") that is located in and forms part of [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] [^src3] [^src1] [^src10] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7]. The clinic is one of many departmental units tracked by the Danish national ADHD quality database (ADHD-databasen), which monitors how well Danish regions and their child and adolescent psychiatric units meet standardized targets for ADHD assessment and treatment processes [^src3] [^src1].

The clinic appears repeatedly in both the 2023 and 2024 annual reports of the ADHD database, which cover the periods 01.04.2023–31.03.2024 and 01.04.2024–31.03.2025 respectively. These reports track a series of quality indicators — including diagnostic conferences (Indicator 3), coordinating network meetings (Indicator 4), somatic examination during assessment, and clinical environment observation for children aged 0–5 — all measured against a national development target of 90% fulfillment. Across the corpus, both the national and regional data reveal chronic underperformance against this benchmark, and Bispebjerg's outpatient clinic is no exception.

In the 2023 report, Bispebjerg: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge opnåede 27 % opfyldelse af Indikator 3 blandt 484 udredningsforløb [^src3], with 132 of those pathways meeting the criterion (95% CI: 23–31) [^src3]. For Indicator 4 (coordinating network meetings held within 90 days of treatment start), Bispebjerg havde 25 % opfyldelse af indikator 4 (95% CI: 16-36) med 20 forløb ud af 81 [^src1], and a related entry recorded 19 of 81 pathways meeting a similar measure at 23% (95% CI: 15–34) [^src2]. On somatic examination, the clinic reported that 310 of 484 assessment pathways (64%) included somatic workup [^src6], and for another related process measure 34 of 54 pathways (63%, 95% CI: 49–76) were recorded [^src7]. The 2023 report also lists the clinic with a raw entry of "3 # #" in an appendix table, where hashed values likely reflect small-sample suppression [^src4], and one mention simply names the clinic without additional figures [^src5].

The 2024 report — covering the following year — shows a similar pattern of mixed and generally low performance. The clinic (listed there under the code B19) recorded 209 of 459 pathways (46%, 95% CI: 41–50) meeting one indicator [^src8], while separate entries show 88 of 499 pathways at 18% (95% CI: 14–21) [^src9] and 84 of 441 pathways at 19% (95% CI: 15–23) [^src10]. Other entries for the same reporting period show 103 of 441 pathways at 23% (95% CI: 19–28) [^src11] and, for a different measure in the same table, 271 of 441 pathways reaching 61% (95% CI: 57–66) [^src11]. For smaller sub-populations, the clinic reported 0 of 8 pathways (0%, 95% CI: 0–37) [^src12] and 3 of 8 pathways (38%, 95% CI: 9–76) [^src13], alongside a bare figure of "37" in a further table [^src14] and a suppressed entry showing "#/#" with a wide confidence interval of 0–98% [^src15].

Taken together, these figures place Bispebjerg's child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinic squarely within the broader national picture documented by the ADHD database: a system in which most indicators fall well short of the 90% development target, reflecting capacity pressures, registration difficulties, and shortages of medical staff across Danish child and adolescent psychiatry [^src3] [^src1] [^src6]. The clinic's results are reported and compared alongside other departments within Region Hovedstaden and the other four Danish regions as part of the database's ongoing effort to track and improve ADHD assessment and treatment quality nationwide.
